ActorPoolAllocator: Internal JSL/JSR allocator that pops the next free actor slot from the LIFO free list at ($4E). On success returns carry clear with Y = new actor WRAM base ($1000 + index×$30) and zeroes the free-list entry; on pool exhaustion returns carry set with Y = $1FC0. Increments activeActorCount on allocation. Called by SpawnSceneActors, AllocateActorBefore/After, and SpawnBefore/After COP handlers.
AdhocVramDma:
COP #4F with a long source Address, a VRAM destination word and a size word (7 operand bytes). First call: if the staging block is free (adhocVramDmaDest = 0) it copies the operands into adhocVramDma / adhocVramDmaBank / adhocVramDmaDest / adhocVramDmaSize, sets extendedFlags bit 0 and yields. Later calls (bit 0 set) compare the COP's destination operand with adhocVramDmaDest, which the NMI zeroes when DmaAdhocVramBlock runs; once they differ the transfer is done, bit 0 is cleared and the script resumes after the 7 operand bytes. If the block is busy with another transfer it yields without staging. Every yield rewinds the actor entry address ($00) to this COP so it runs again next frame.

The destination word is written before the size word, but the NMI fires on a nonzero destination (see OQ-45).
AdvanceMapY: Internal JSR helper that advances the collision map index in $001C by one tile row ($10 bytes within a page). When the low byte overflows (the row nibble wrapped past 15) it adds mapRowStrideL0 to a page byte taken from the accumulator's hidden high half (the caller's last 16-bit A, inferred to be the page of the last tile written; not reloaded from $1C), moving to the first row of the next page row. This matches the intended result only while the rectangle's row does not cross a page edge horizontally; ClearCollisionRect and its Full variant use a 16-bit ADC of mapBoundsX instead, which does not have this dependency. Called by MarkCollisionRect between rectangle rows.
AdvanceSpriteAnim: COP #56 with no operands. Indexes the spriteset table by anim index ($28) and frame counter ($2A), stages sprite-tile DMA via animScratch, and RTL while DMA is pending ($00B2); clears $2A and RTI when the frame sequence ends (negative entry).
AllocateActorAfter:
Allocate a slot and insert it after the current actor (X = D = current), then CopyActorState.

Returns Y = new actor; if the new actor has no next it becomes the list tail ($58). If the pool is exhausted nothing is linked.
AllocateActorBefore:
Allocate a slot and insert it before the current actor (X = D = current), then CopyActorState.

Returns Y = new actor. If the pool is exhausted (carry set from the allocator) nothing is linked and the routine returns at once.
AllocateSpecialActor:
Allocate a thinker slot (ThinkerPoolAlloc) and append it to the thinker list (tail in $5C); returns Y = new thinker.

No CopyActorState: only prev/next are linked and $06/$08 are zeroed. Allocation failure (carry set) returns without linking.
AndExtraFlags: COP #5C with one word operand. ANDs the actor's extendedFlags word ($7F002A) with the operand, so the operand is a mask of bits to KEEP (e.g. #$FFF7 clears bit 3).
AnimFrameLookup:
Internal JSR helper: A = movement index → A = movement_delta_table[A×2].

The returned word is the head pointer of a movement delta chain (a linked list of signed per-frame deltas), not a frame duration. Callers store it in $2C (X chain) or $2E (Y chain): StageMoveX/Y/XY, ForceDirSW/NE/Both and ReloadMoveDurations in cop_handlers_force_move.
AnimLoop: COP #8A with no operands. Repeats UpdateActorAnimation until a cycle completes, then decrements sprTimer and loops the animation until the timer reaches zero before clearing deltas and continuing.
AnimOnce: COP #89 with no operands. Calls UpdateActorAnimation each frame, yielding RTL while animation is in progress; on completion clears movement deltas $2C/$2E and RTI.
AnimOneFrame: COP #8B with no operands. Calls UpdateActorAnimation once and always RTI; clears $2C/$2E if the animation sequence finished that frame.
ApplyBgChange: COP #33 with no operands. Renders one frame (UpdateFrameRender + UpdateFrameDialogue), then loops AnimateEventBlock — each call swaps tiles and queues the on-screen ones for VRAM until the queue is full or all tiles are done — with an UpdateFrameDialogue frame between calls to flush the queue. Carry set from AnimateEventBlock = all tiles processed. Ends with one more frame.
ApplyFollowMovement:
Adds the step in $0000 (X) and $0002 (Y) to this actor's position ($14/$16) and copies the new position to the prev-link actor (the spawner), so the spawner moves with the helper. The step is also stored in moveScratch1/2, which the spawner scripts read back.

If the dither phase in orbitDiameter is 8 or more, it is cleared and the helper re-aims next frame (JumpNextFrame to FollowChaseMainLoop). Otherwise RTL ends the frame and the actor resumes at the SetEntryHere inside its handler, repeating the same heading with the next dither window.
ApplyMoveToChild: COP #B0 with two byte operands (X index, Y index). Same staging as StageMoveXY, but written to the newest actor in the list (actorListLast, $0058) rather than the caller, so spawn the child immediately before it. The caller's slot is saved with PHY and restored with PLX.
ApplyScrollOffset: Add the next stream record, an X word and a Y word, to this actor's position ($14/$16); the stream pointer ($0650) advances by 4.
BindSineHdma: COP #61 with a long Address (table base word + bank byte, e.g. $7E8800) and a byte channel-config index (hdma_channel_config entry, #0D–#10 observed). Adds $0200 to the table address on odd frames ($0036 bit 0, the double buffer), then calls SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect with Y = table address and A = bank byte | index << 8.
bitmasks_bit_position: Shared 8-byte lookup table mapping bit indices 0–7 to single-bit mask bytes: $01, $02, $04, $08, $10, $20, $40, $80. Used by all Set/Clear/Test flag routines for bit-level access to the eventFlags and wramFlags arrays.
BossClearApplyStatReward:
Iterates enemy_clear_reward_table entries in the boss's range [$04.lo .. $0E].
Each entry byte is a reward type: 1=MaxHP+1, 2=STR+1, 3=DEF+1, 0=skip.
Uses per-enemy flags ($0300 range) to avoid granting the same reward twice.
BranchIfActorAt: COP #29 with one byte (actor list index), two words (X, Y), and one &Code operand. Resolves the actor via ResolveActorIndex then performs the same exact pixel coordinate compare as BranchIfPlayerAt.
BranchIfActorNear:
COP #20 with one byte (actor list index), one byte (radius) and one &Code operand. Resolves the actor via ResolveActorIndex ($1000 + index × $30) and branches if both |ΔX| and |ΔY| are ≤ radius × 16 px (the code compares against radius × 16 + 1); otherwise skips the branch address.

No script in extracted/ uses this COP.
BranchIfBehindWall:
COP #5D wall-occlusion branch taking one &Code operand. Converts the actor pixel position to tile coordinates, samples the collision layer via CalcTileMapOffset, and decides whether the tile hides the actor. If the actor is behind a wall (high nibble set, or a low nibble other than 0 or $0E, or the position is out of the map), the script jumps to the branch target; if it is visible, the operand is skipped and the script continues. The branch is taken on occlusion, as the COP name says.

When bit 4 of byte $0F of the actor (the high byte of oamXorFlags $0E; that is OAM attribute priority bit 0, inferred) is set, the handler takes the "layer-aware" path, where both outcomes of the tile test lead to "visible", so only the out-of-map check can occlude. Used by Eyesore, the diamond-mine enemies, and similar actors.
BranchIfBodyNe: COP #49 (id 73), no users. One byte (form ID) plus a &Code target: branches when characterForm ($0AD4) is not equal to the byte; when equal it skips the 2-byte target.
BranchIfCollisionTypeNe: COP #62 with one byte (collision type nibble) and one &Code branch target. Samples the collision layer at the actor's tile via CalcTileMapOffset; jumps to the branch target when the tile's low nibble EQUALS the operand or the position is out of bounds, otherwise skips the branch operand. The COP name BranchIfCollisionTypeNe says "not equal" but the code branches on equality (BEQ). The solid nibble is ignored: a solid tile whose low nibble matches also branches. The operand is stored in absolute $0000 (global scratch) before D is zeroed, then compared with CMP $00, which reads the same location.
BranchIfDirToPlayer: COP #2F with one byte (direction) and one &Code operand. Branches if ComputeDirectionToPlayer from the actor matches the operand direction; otherwise skips the branch address.
BranchIfDirToPlayerFrom: COP #30 with two signed byte offsets (X, Y), one byte (direction), and one &Code operand. Same as BranchIfDirToPlayer but computes direction from an offset reference point added to the actor position.
BranchIfHasItem: COP #D6 with one byte (item ID) and one &Code operand. Calls CheckInventoryForItem; branches to the &Code offset when the item is present (carry clear = found).
BranchIfItemEquipped: COP #D7 with one byte (item ID) and one &Code operand. Compares the operand against inventorySlots[inventoryEquippedIndex]; branches to &Code when they match. inventorySlots is a 16-byte array ($0AB4–$0AC3, one item ID per byte; CheckInventoryForItem steps it with INY), so the index is a plain byte index. When nothing is equipped (index $FFFF, e.g. after RemoveItem) the indexed read wraps to $0AB3 — the byte before the array — so the compare reads unrelated data (analysis only, unverified at runtime).
BranchIfNotOnGridline: COP #1F with one &Code operand. Branches when the actor is off the 16-pixel grid: either its Y has a non-zero low nibble, or its X plus the metasprite hitbox X offset (hitbox byte 0, forced negative by ORA #$FF00) has one. Falls through (operand skipped) only when both are aligned. DBR is switched to the sprite-data bank ($7F0008,X) to read the hitbox header and restored on both exits.
BranchIfNotPressed: COP #41 with one word (button mask, bit 0 selects joypadRaw) plus one &Code branch target. Jumps to the target when none of the masked buttons is down in the selected source, otherwise skips the target operand. Inverse of BranchIfPressed.
BranchIfOffCamera: COP #68 with one &Code operand. Compares the actor position ($14 = X, $16 = Y) against the camera window: cameraOffsetX/Y (left/top limit) and cameraBoundsX/Y (right/bottom limit), the active map window's scroll limits per docs/wram-memory-map.md. If both axes are inside the window the operand is skipped and the script continues; otherwise the script jumps to the operand. A negative position counts as outside, the lower limit is inclusive and the upper limit exclusive (position ≥ limit = outside). Used by enemy scripts (e.g. awB0_zip_fly, pyD2_haunt, gw83_asp, gw82_fire_bug, av6D_dive_bat).
BranchIfPlayerAt: COP #28 with two words (X, Y) and one &Code operand. Branches if the player's exact pixel coordinates match the operand position; otherwise skips the branch address.
BranchIfPlayerInAbsTiles:
COP #45 (copdef id 69): absolute tile-rectangle branch. Operands: four bytes in the order minX, minY, maxX, maxY (absolute tile coordinates) plus a &Code target.

Each byte is multiplied by 16 and compared with the player actor's position. The tested point is (player.X, player.Y − 8): inside when minX×16 < X ≤ maxX×16 and minY×16 < Y−8 ≤ maxY×16. The adjusted Y is kept in scratch $0000. Inside → jump to the target; otherwise skip the six-byte operand block.
BranchIfPlayerInRelTiles:
COP #44 (copdef id 68): relative tile-rectangle branch. Operands: four signed bytes in the order minX, minY, maxX, maxY (tiles, relative to this actor) plus a &Code target.

Each byte is sign-extended, multiplied by 16 (ASL ×4) and added to the actor's own X ($14) or Y ($16). The player is inside when minX < player.X ≤ maxX and minY < player.Y ≤ maxY (unsigned compares on the player actor's $14/$16). Inside → jump to the target; otherwise skip the six-byte operand block (4 bytes + &Code).
BranchIfPlayerNear: COP #21 with one byte (radius) and one &Code operand. Shares the square proximity test of BranchIfActorNear but compares against playerActor.
BranchIfPressed: COP #40 with one word (button mask, bit 0 selects joypadRaw) plus one &Code branch target (same bank as the script). Jumps to the target if any masked button is down, otherwise skips the two-byte target. Never yields; used heavily by the player actor (walk, ladder and shimmy state machines).
BranchIfSolidEast: COP #18 with one &Code operand. Queries the tile one column east (X + $10) and branches on the same solid-nibble test pattern.
BranchIfSolidHere: COP #13 with one &Code operand. Probes the actor's own tile with TileCollisionQuery and branches to the target when the result has any bit of $000F set: the tile is blocked (high nibble set), the probe is outside the camera bounds, or the tile's terrain type is non-zero. Otherwise the operand is skipped. The same $000F test is used by the directional variants (#15–#18).
BranchIfSolidNorth: COP #15 with one &Code operand. Queries the tile one row north (Y − $10) via TileCollisionQuery and branches to the script offset when the result has any lower-nibble bit set.
BranchIfSolidOffset: COP #14 with two signed byte tile offsets plus one &Code operand. Sign-extends and ×16-scales each offset, adds them to the actor position, runs TileCollisionQuery at the resulting pixel position, and branches on the same $000F test as BranchIfSolidHere. It repeats the offset math of ParseSignedTileOffset inline but keeps pixel units (TileCollisionQuery does the tile conversion and its own −1 row adjustment).
BranchIfSolidSouth: COP #16 with one &Code operand. Queries the tile one row south (Y + $10) and branches on the same lower-nibble solid test as BranchIfSolidHere.
BranchIfSolidType: COP #1A (copdef name BranchIfSolidType) with one byte (expected type) plus one &Code operand. TileCollisionQuery at the actor position; branches if the low byte of the result equals the operand. Blocked and out-of-bounds probes return $0F, so they match an operand of $0F. On a mismatch the pushed result is popped into Y (Y is clobbered; X and D still hold the slot).
BranchIfSolidTypeEast: COP #1E with one byte type and one &Code operand. Compares collision type at X + $10 and branches to &Code on match.
BranchIfSolidTypeNorth: COP #1B with one byte type and one &Code operand. Compares the collision type at Y − $10 against the operand and branches on equality.
BranchIfSolidTypeSouth: COP #1C with one byte type and one &Code operand. Same type comparison as BranchIfSolidType but samples the tile at Y + $10.
BranchIfSolidTypeWest: COP #1D with one byte type and one &Code operand. Compares collision type at X − $10 and branches to &Code on match.
BranchIfSolidWest: COP #17 with one &Code operand. Queries the tile one column west (X − $10) and branches if TileCollisionQuery reports a set lower-nibble bit.
BranchNearerAxis: COP #2C with two &Code operands. Compares |ΔX| and |ΔY| to the player: operand[0] when |ΔY| < |ΔX| (horizontal separation dominates), operand[1] when |ΔY| ≥ |ΔX| (vertical dominates or tie).
BranchOnFlagByte: COP #D0 with one byte (flag), one byte (sense), and one &Code operand. Tests the flag via TestEventFlag; the sense byte selects branch-on-set vs branch-on-clear, jumping to the &Code offset when the condition matches.
BranchOnFlagWord: COP #D1 with one word (flag), one byte (sense), and one &Code operand. Word-indexed variant of BranchOnFlagByte with the same sense-controlled conditional branch.
BranchOnPlayerFacing: COP #31 with four &Code operands. Calls GetPlayerFacingDirection (0 = down, 1 = up, 2 = left, 3 = right) and branches to operand[facing]. If the player has no facing (carry set, value ≥ 4) the 8 operand bytes are skipped.
BranchOnPlayerX: COP #2A with one word (threshold) and three &Code addresses (west, center, east). Three-way branch on horizontal player offset: zero delta → center, |ΔX| within threshold → center, beyond threshold → west or east.
BranchOnPlayerY: COP #2B with one word (threshold) and three &Code addresses (above, center, below). Same three-way logic as BranchOnPlayerX but compares vertical player offset on Y.
BuildSineHdmaTable:
Internal JSR helper that fills two interleaved HDMA indirect-data tables with per-scanline scroll offsets derived from sine_table_8bit.

Computes a double-buffered WRAM table base from spritesetPtr + $0100, ping-ponging by $0200 on $0036 bit 0 (frame parity). Divides $0100 by the wave period n (half of the byte count in actor $0E) to get the sine angle step per scanline, then iterates over the n scanlines of one period: looks up sine_table_8bit at the current angle, multiplies by actor amplitude ($7F0008) via SNES hardware multiply, handles sign correction for negative sine values, and writes camera-offset scroll values into both horizontal ($62) and vertical ($5E) HDMA data regions.

Called by TickSineHdma with camera coordinates in DP $18 (X) and $1C (Y). Operates in data bank $7E with DP zeroed. Returns via RTS.
BuildSineLookupTable:
Internal helper that fills the 512-byte sineTableA ($7E8900) and sineTableB ($7E8B00) arrays with amplitude-scaled sine values.

Guard conditions: proceeds only if displayModeFlags bit 6 ($0040) is set or animScratch2 bit 0 ($0001) is set; clears the trigger bit after acknowledging it. This ensures tables are only regenerated when flagged as needed by the HDMA system.

Reads actor amplitude from $7F0008 into WRMPYA, then iterates 256 word entries: looks up each sine sample from sine_table_8bit at step intervals of $0E, multiplies by amplitude via hardware multiply, corrects negative samples (multiply RDMPYH by $FF, add RDMPYL for sign extension), and writes the scaled 16-bit result to both sineTableA and sineTableB at the same index.

Called by GenHdmaSine (COP #00) to populate the full sine tables used by HDMA wave effects. Returns via RTS.
CallNear: COP #C8 with one &Code operand. Saves the current return PC in retPtr1, then RTI-jumps to the same-bank &Code target.
CallNearDeferred: COP #C9 with one &Code operand. Sets $00 to the target &Code offset, saves the return PC in retPtr1, and yields via RTL so the callee runs next frame.
CameraPanDown: COP #DC (script name PanCameraDown) southward camera pan with no operands. Decrements the frame counter $2A each call; when it underflows, loads the next scroll-table word with CameraScrollStepLookup (low byte → $2A, high byte → $2B; a zero high byte ends the table and the script resumes). Each call adds the low nibble of $2B to cameraTargetY. Yields via PLA PLA RTL until cameraTargetY reaches cameraBoundsY, then resumes the script. Called from forced_walk and other cutscene scroll actors.
CameraPanLeft: COP #DF with no operands. Decrements $2A, reloads the step word with CameraScrollStepLookup, subtracts the step in $2B (low nibble) from cameraTargetX, and yields until cameraTargetX drops below cameraOffsetX. If the step would exceed the current cameraTargetX the script resumes without storing it.
CameraPanRight: COP #DE with no operands. Decrements $2A, reloads the step word with CameraScrollStepLookup, adds the step in $2B (low nibble) to cameraTargetX, and yields until cameraTargetX reaches cameraBoundsX.
CameraPanUp: COP #DD with no operands. Mirrors CameraPanDown: decrements $2A, reloads the step word with CameraScrollStepLookup, subtracts the step in $2B (low nibble) from cameraTargetY, and yields until cameraTargetY drops below cameraOffsetY. If the step would exceed the current cameraTargetY the script resumes without storing it.
CameraScrollStepLookup: Reads the next scroll speed entry from the table at scrollStepTableBase, indexed by scrollStepIndex. Increments the index and doubles it for word access. Returns carry clear with the speed value in A when the entry high byte is non-zero (valid step); returns carry set and resets scrollStepIndex to zero when a zero high-byte terminator is reached. Called by all four CameraPan handlers (Down/Up/Right/Left) to fetch per-frame scroll step values.
CardinalToPlayer:
COP #35 with no operands. Returns Y/A = 0 north, 1 east, 2 south, 3 west, picking the axis with the larger |Δ|; ties go to north/south. This is not the order of GetPlayerFacingDirection.

Uses an RTS trick: the handler pushes CardinalToPlayer_Exit−1 and every exit path is an RTS into CardinalToPlayer_Exit, which stores the script PC and returns Y in A.
CardinalToPlayer_Exit: Shared exit of CardinalToPlayer, reached by RTS: stores the script PC ($0A) as the return PC and returns the direction (Y) in A via RTI.
ClearAllWramFlags:
JSL helper that zero-fills the $20-byte wramFlags block ($0A80–$0A9F, event flags $0400–$04FF) with a word loop (16 iterations).

Callers: WorldMapController (twice, when the world map is entered), st68_kara and sp58_red_eye; game_over_sequence clears the same $20 bytes inline on a true death. No call at ordinary scene changes was found (OQ-67).
ClearCollisionHere: COP #11 with no operands. Calls ClearCollisionRect with flag $0001, which routes to ClearCollisionRectFull and ANDs #$00 on every hitbox tile to zero both solid and type nibbles.
ClearCollisionRect: Internal JSR helper that clears solid flags from a rectangle on the collision map. Reads the metasprite hitbox exactly like MarkCollisionRect, then ANDs #$0F on every tile in the rectangle to remove the solid nibble while preserving the type nibble. If the flag word in WRAM $0000 is nonzero it jumps to ClearCollisionRectFull instead. Row stepping is inlined: +$10 on the low byte, and on carry the page byte is advanced by adding the word mapBoundsX (see the note at that ADC). Called by ClearSolidHere (flag 0) and ClearCollisionHere (flag 1).
ClearCollisionRectFull: Internal subroutine reached via JMP from ClearCollisionRect when the full-clear flag ($0001) is set. ANDs #$00 on every tile in the metasprite hitbox rectangle, zeroing both the solid and type nibbles. Used by ClearCollisionHere to completely remove collision data at the actor footprint.
ClearEventFlag: Core JSR routine that clears one bit in the eventFlags ($0A00) bitfield. Loads the bitmasks_bit_position entry, inverts it via EOR #$FF to create a clear mask, then ANDs against the eventFlags byte. Called by ClearFlag COP handlers and JSL wrappers.
ClearFlag_0100: JSL helper that clears event/trigger flag $0100 + (A AND $FF). No caller was found in the extracted code.
ClearFlagByte: COP #CE with one byte operand. Calls ClearEventFlag on the byte flag index.
ClearFlagRaw: JSL helper that clears an event flag without adding a base offset. Masks to byte and calls ClearEventFlag directly.
ClearFlagWord: COP #CF with one word operand. Calls ClearEventFlag on the word flag index.
ClearHMirror: COP #BA with no operands. Clears horizontal mirror bit $4000 on OAM attribute word $0E via TRB.
ClearPriorityMax: COP #B4 with no operands. Clears bit $0002 on actor+$10 via TRB, removing the front-most override (Y-based sorting resumes unless bit $0001 is set).
ClearPriorityMin: COP #B5 with no operands. Clears bit $0001 on actor+$10 via TRB, removing the rear-most override (Y-based sorting resumes unless bit $0002 is set).
ClearSolidAbs: COP #10 with two byte operands (absolute tile X and Y). Resolves the map index and ANDs #$0F on that collisionLayer byte to remove solid flags.
ClearSolidHere: COP #0C with no operands. Copies the actor pixel position into the probe scratch $18/$1C and calls ClearCollisionRect with flag $0000, ANDing #$0F on every collisionLayer tile in the metasprite hitbox to clear the solid nibble while preserving the terrain type nibble.
ClearSolidOffset: COP #0E with two signed byte tile offsets. Uses the same ParseSignedTileOffset path as MarkSolidOffset, then ANDs #$0F on one collisionLayer tile to clear the solid nibble only.
ClearTypeAbs: COP #12 with two byte operands (absolute tile X and Y). Converts to a map index and ANDs #$F0 on the collision byte, clearing only the type nibble while leaving solid flags intact.
ComputeDirectionToPlayer: Internal JSR helper that computes an 8-direction octant index (0–7) from the reference point in $0018/$001C (pixels) to the player position. Compass order is clockwise from north: 0=N, 1=NE, 2=E, 3=SE, 4=S, 5=SW, 6=W, 7=NW (not the same numbering as GetPlayerFacingDirection). Rule: if |ΔY| < $10 the result is pure E or W whatever ΔX is (including the player standing on the reference point, which gives E); otherwise the vertical component is N or S, and it becomes a diagonal only when |ΔX| ≥ $10. Returns the octant in A. Called by DirToPlayer, DirToPlayerFrom, BranchIfDirToPlayer and BranchIfDirToPlayerFrom (cop_handlers_player_query).
ComputeFollowAngle:
Slope row for a Y-dominant aim (|dy| ≥ |dx|), stored in orbitAngle (0 = 45 degrees … 16 = axis-aligned).

Inputs: $0018 = |dx|, $001C = |dy| (set by FollowChaseMainLoop or smooth_follow_child). Equal deltas give row 0. Otherwise q = |dx| / (|dy| >> 4) ≈ 16·|dx|/|dy| using the hardware divide (UnsignedDivide, Y = dividend, A = divisor; a |dy| below 16 uses divisor 1), folded into a row: q ≥ $18 → 32 − q, $11-$17 → q − 16, ≤ $10 → 16 − q. Clears orbitDiameter (dither phase) and returns with RTS.
ComputeFollowAngleAlt: Same as ComputeFollowAngle with the axes swapped, for an X-dominant aim (|dx| > |dy|): q = |dy| / (|dx| >> 4). The shared tail (divide, fold, store) is in the sub-labels of this block.
ComputeFollowStep: Produces this frame's step: $0000 = loopCounter (major-axis pixels) and $0002 = minor-axis pixels = the sum of the next loopCounter words (each 0 or 1) of FollowSlopeDitherTable row orbitAngle, starting at column orbitDiameter and wrapping at 16. The new phase (old + loopCounter) & 15 is stored back in orbitDiameter. Scratch: $0004 column counter, $0006/$0008 start and end phase. Also called directly by smooth_follow_child.
ComputeScrollDeltas:
Computes the scroll delta for both axes with the hardware multiply/divide unit.

For each axis: A = the packed ratio in $14 (X) or $16 (Y), Y = cameraTargetX ($06BE) or cameraTargetY ($06C2); calls hardware_math.MulDivide via JSL, which returns (A low byte × Y) ÷ A high byte, and stores it in cameraDeltaX ($06C0) or cameraDeltaY ($06C4).

If the packed value is 0 the MulDivide call and the store are skipped and that axis keeps its previous delta.
cop_dispatch_table:
227-entry handler pointer table: COP opcodes $00–$6D and $80–$E2 (209 valid, ids match copdef.json) to short-address handler labels in 30 handler blocks. Opcodes $6E–$7F are an 18-entry #$0000 gap.

Handler labels that differ from the copdef script names: $1A–$1E BranchIfType* = BranchIfSolidType*; $80–$87 StageSpriteFrame* = StageSprite* (Frame, MoveX/Y/XY, Loop, LoopMoveX/Y/XY); $8F–$92 StagePlayerSprite/MoveX/MoveY/MoveXY = StagePlayerSprite and StagePlayerMoveX/Y/XY; $B6/$B7 SetSpritePriority/SetSpritePalette = SetSpritePriority/SetSpritePalette.
cop_table_sentinel: NOP/BRA loop placed right after the table. It is not an effective guard: an opcode ≥ $E3 would index past the table and JMP (table,X) would read the sentinel's own code bytes as a pointer (opcode $E3 reads EA 80 = $80EA) instead of jumping to the loop. No script is known to use such opcodes.
CopDispatch:
Central COP dispatcher reached from CopVector.

Sets X = Y = actor ID (Y keeps it for handlers), $0C = bank byte from the COP stack frame and $0A = pushed PC − 1 (the COP signature byte, which is the opcode), reads the opcode, advances $0A past it, and jumps through cop_dispatch_table[opcode × 2].
CopVector: COP software interrupt vector. Jumps to the COP dispatch handler which implements the game's scripting command system.
CopyActorState:
Initialise the new actor Y from the spawner X (= D). See the file header for the field list.

$10: ORA #$2000 forces that bit on and AND #$F7FC clears $0803 (bit meanings: OQ-60). $12: clears $1000 (runs in display-filter mode). $0024 receives the spawner's slot (OQ-65). Zeroes parentId, $2C/$2E, moveScratch1/2, $08 and chatPtr; extendedFlags and the callback block are zeroed only when sceneCurrent ≠ $FF.
CopyPalette: COP #50 with a long source Address (word + bank), a byte source color index, a byte destination color index and a byte color count. Copies count colors from source + 2 × srcIndex to cgramPalette ($7F0A00) + 2 × dstIndex with the RAM MVN stub at $0402: source bank → $0405, destination bank $7F → $0404, X = source, Y = destination, A = bytes − 1.
CopyPosToNext: COP #47 (id 71), no operands, no users. Copies this actor's pixel position ($14/$16) to its next linked actor ($06); shares the copy code with CopyPosToPrev. No null check.
CopyPosToPrev: COP #46 (id 70), no operands, no users. Copies this actor's pixel position ($14/$16) to its previous linked actor ($04). No null check: with no previous actor ($04 = 0) it would write to WRAM $0014/$0016.
CopySiblingFollowState:
Entry for helpers whose spawner has already set the follow parameters.

Copies loopCounter (speed) and chatPtr (animation base) from the prev-link actor ($0004,Y — the spawner, because SpawnAfterMarked inserts the new actor right after it) into this actor, then enters FollowChaseMainLoop. Unlike InitFollowAndChase it leaves animScratch2 alone, so the spawner can preset the initial facing (mu5F_flasher stores $26 there before the helper first runs).
Decompress: COP #51 with a long source Address (word + bank) and a long destination Address. Only the destination word is used: the WRAM output buffer address (bank $7E, e.g. mode7Tilemap or mapLayerTilemap); its bank byte is read and discarded. Stores the source in $3E/$40 and the output address in $7A for QuintetLzDecompress, reads the 2-byte size header (decompressed byte count) into $78, decompresses, then calls ClearActorRenderList before resuming the script.
DialogueOptions:
COP #BE with two byte operands (read together as one word and passed to MenuSelectionHandler as its menu parameters, e.g. the grid encoding; not a pointer) plus one word (branch table base).

Requires worldReadyFlag == $000F (otherwise it rewinds the script pointer and yields). Sets displayModeFlags bit 13 ($2000; no reader of this bit was found), sets joypadMaskInv = $0F00 (the D-pad buttons are the auto-repeat ones while the menu is open), clears joypadMaskStd and actor $10 bit 11 for the duration, calls MenuSelectionHandler, and branches through the table entry for the chosen option (table base + choice × 2).
Die: COP #E0 with no operands. If actor flag bit $0040 on $12 is set, routes through DieExit to cascade-remove linked child actors by parentId match; otherwise calls UnlinkActor directly. Returns via RTL to terminate the script.
DieExit:
Cascade child-actor removal for Die/MarkDeath when actor flag $0040 is set.

The entry point (PLA/TAX/TCD/PLA/PLA/RTL) is the normal non-child Die exit. The shared cascade at UnlinkChildrenCascade walks the doubly-linked actor list backward ($04 pointers) and forward ($06 pointers) from the dying actor, stopping at the first actor on each side whose parentId does not match the dying actor (the backward and forward boundaries). It then returns every slot strictly between the two boundaries (the children and the dying actor itself) via ReturnActorSlot and patches the list pointers with three cases: head-removed (new head = forward boundary), tail-removed (new tail = backward boundary), or mid-list splice (link the boundaries to each other). Finally it points the dying actor's own next pointer ($06) at the forward boundary so the actor run loop continues past the removed span.
DirToPlayer: COP #2D with no operands. Sets reference coordinates from the actor's $14/$16 and returns a 0–7 octant direction in A via ComputeDirectionToPlayer.
DirToPlayerFrom: COP #2E with two signed byte operands (X, Y pixel offsets). Adds sign-extended offsets to the actor position as the reference point and returns 0–7 direction via ComputeDirectionToPlayer.
DrawMetatileAbs: COP #4B metatile painter taking three byte operands: absolute tile X, tile Y, and metatile ID. Passes through TileQueryGate (RTL early-out if a tile query is already pending), converts tile coords to pixel positions, and calls ResolveTileData to update mapLayerTilemap and collisionLayer and queue BG VRAM tile writes when the target lies on screen. Used heavily in puzzle rooms and mine collapse scenes to swap floor/wall tiles.
DrawMetatileHere: COP #4C with one byte operand (metatile ID). Uses the actor's pixel position ($14/$16), passes TileQueryGate, then calls ResolveTileData to write mapLayerTilemap/collisionLayer and queue on-screen BG VRAM tile updates.
effect_position_update:
Integrating scroll actor that advances forced camera motion with hard bounds.

Each tick converts actor coordinates to velocity ($2C/$2E), adds effectDeltaX/Y, clamps cameraDeltaX against effectBoundsX and cameraDeltaY against effectBoundsY, then writes render deltas to $06E8/$06EA. Pairs with effect_velocity_init and effect_subpixel_math in the visual_effect_pipeline block.
effect_subpixel_math:
Per-frame subpixel scroll refinement actor spawned alongside effect_position_update.

On entry calls SetEntryHere and accumulates fractional scroll: when $14 has a nonzero high byte it scales through hardware_math.MulDivide against cameraTargetX into forcedScrollOverride; otherwise sign-extends and adds the low byte directly. Used in Sky Garden viper lair and mystic-statue sequences for smooth cinematic pans.
effect_velocity_init:
Visual-effect actor that seeds forced camera scroll from actor placement coordinates.

Converts actor $14/$16 (pixel position) into signed scroll velocities at $2C/$2E, zeroes integrated position state, waits one frame, then adds effectDeltaX/Y from the camera_scroll_controller and writes forcedScrollOverride ($06C8) with bit 15 set. Spawned in Babel Tower plane-jump and other cutscene scenes.
EnemyGemDropRouter:
Gem-type dispatcher called from StandardEnemyDefeatHandler when the enemy's stats byte at offset $03 is nonzero and scene flag $0300 is clear.

Uses the kill-count value in orbitAngle: two DEC operations select among three DarkGemDropSystem spawn targets (type 1, type 2, or weighted random). Each path spawns a gem actor via SpawnLastRel then jumps back for the remainder of the defeat sequence.
ExecuteVramDma:
Executes a single VRAM DMA transfer using pre-staged parameters.

Reads transfer parameters from direct page:
- $00B2: byte count (0 = skip)
- $00B0: VRAM destination address
- $00AC-$00AE: ROM/RAM source address (16-bit + bank)

Triggers DMA channel 0 and clears the byte count to prevent re-triggering.
FadeThenStartMusic: COP #05 with one byte operand (music bundle ID). Same allocation, $12/$10 flag handling and chatPtr as StartMusic, but the thinker's entry is SpcCheckMusicReady: it sends $F1 on APUIO0, waits for the echo, sends $01, and falls into SpcTransferMusicData when the SPC answers zero. That routine contains no fade step (OQ-61).
field_reveal_flash: Flash effect: plays reveal SFX and animates one flash sprite frame, then dies.
field_reveal_scatter:
Scatter particle: randomizes position using range from parent ($20=X range, $22=Y range).
Range tiers: 0-1 = ±$0F, 2-3 = ±$1F, 4+ = ±$3F pixels. LSR+carry sets sign (50/50 ±).
follow_fallback_table: Apply halves (the code after each COP SetEntryHere) of the eight octant handlers, indexed by heading − 1: N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW.
FollowChaseHeadESE:
Octant handler: target down-right, |dx| > |dy|. The actor heads mostly EAST.

Slope row from ComputeFollowAngleAlt, facing base 4 (E, ESE, SE) via ResolveFollowDirection, step X += major, Y += minor. If the facing is still turning ($0000 not negative) the actor continues along its current facing through SelectFallbackDirection instead. (The eight FollowChaseHead* handlers are named for the heading they produce: ESE, SSE, SSW, WSW, WNW, NNW, NNE, ENE.)
FollowChaseHeadNNW:
Octant handler: target up-left, |dy| ≥ |dx|. The actor heads mostly NORTH.

ComputeFollowAngle, facing base $E (NW, NNW, N) via ResolveFollowDirectionAlt, step X −= minor, Y −= major. Its apply half runs straight on into ApplyFollowMovement.
FollowChaseHeadSSE:
Octant handler: target down-right, |dy| ≥ |dx|. The actor heads mostly SOUTH.

ComputeFollowAngle, facing base 6 (SE, SSE, S) via ResolveFollowDirectionAlt, step swapped: X += minor, Y += major.
FollowChaseHeadSSW:
Octant handler: target down-left, |dy| ≥ |dx|. The actor heads mostly SOUTH.

ComputeFollowAngle, facing base 8 (S, SSW, SW) via ResolveFollowDirection, step X −= minor, Y += major.
FollowChaseHeadWNW:
Octant handler: target up-left, |dx| > |dy|. The actor heads mostly WEST.

ComputeFollowAngleAlt, facing base $C (W, WNW, NW) via ResolveFollowDirection, step X −= major, Y −= minor.
FollowChaseHeadWSW:
Octant handler: target down-left, |dx| > |dy|. The actor heads mostly WEST.

ComputeFollowAngleAlt, facing base $A (SW, WSW, W) via ResolveFollowDirectionAlt, step X −= major, Y += minor.
FollowDirectionTable: One handler per facing frame (animScratch2 & 15), clockwise from north: N, NNE, NE, ENE, E, ESE, SE, SSE, S, SSW, SW, WSW, W, WNW, NW, NNW. ResolveFollowDirection pushes the entry minus one and RTSes into it.
FollowDirHandler00: Facing N (frame 0): clears the spawner’s OAM mirror bits (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 1 and slope row $10 (axis-aligned), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving N. Handlers 00-0F differ only in these constants.
FollowDirHandler01: Facing NNE (frame 1): clears the spawner’s OAM mirror bits (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 1 and slope row $08 (half slope), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving NNE.
FollowDirHandler02: Facing NE (frame 2): clears the spawner’s OAM mirror bits (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 2 and slope row $00 (45 degrees), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving NE.
FollowDirHandler03: Facing ENE (frame 3): clears the spawner’s OAM mirror bits (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 2 and slope row $08 (half slope), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving ENE.
FollowDirHandler04: Facing E (frame 4): clears the spawner’s OAM mirror bits (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 3 and slope row $10 (axis-aligned), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving E.
FollowDirHandler05: Facing ESE (frame 5): sets V-mirror ($8000) on the spawner (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 3 and slope row $08 (half slope), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving ESE.
FollowDirHandler06: Facing SE (frame 6): sets V-mirror ($8000) on the spawner (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 4 and slope row $00 (45 degrees), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving SE.
FollowDirHandler07: Facing SSE (frame 7): sets V-mirror ($8000) on the spawner (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 4 and slope row $08 (half slope), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving SSE.
FollowDirHandler08: Facing S (frame 8): sets V-mirror ($8000) on the spawner (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 5 and slope row $10 (axis-aligned), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving S.
FollowDirHandler09: Facing SSW (frame 9): sets H+V mirror ($C000) on the spawner (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 5 and slope row $08 (half slope), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving SSW.
FollowDirHandler0A: Facing SW (frame 10): sets H+V mirror ($C000) on the spawner (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 6 and slope row $00 (45 degrees), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving SW.
FollowDirHandler0B: Facing WSW (frame 11): sets H+V mirror ($C000) on the spawner (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 6 and slope row $08 (half slope), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving WSW.
FollowDirHandler0C: Facing W (frame 12): sets H-mirror ($4000) on the spawner (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 7 and slope row $10 (axis-aligned), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving W.
FollowDirHandler0D: Facing WNW (frame 13): sets H-mirror ($4000) on the spawner (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 7 and slope row $08 (half slope), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving WNW.
FollowDirHandler0E: Facing NW (frame 14): sets H-mirror ($4000) on the spawner (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 8 and slope row $00 (45 degrees), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving NW.
FollowDirHandler0F: Facing NNW (frame 15): sets H-mirror ($4000) on the spawner (skipped when carry = chatPtr bit 15). While the facing is still turning it sets heading 8 and slope row $08 (half slope), so SelectFallbackDirection keeps the actor moving NNW.
FollowSlopeDitherTable:
Dither table for ComputeFollowStep: 17 rows (orbitAngle 0 = 45 degrees ... 16 = axis-aligned) of 16 words, each 0 or 1.

ComputeFollowStep sums a window of loopCounter entries starting at the dither phase (orbitDiameter); that count is the minor-axis pixels moved this frame. Row 0 is all 1s (equal axes); later rows have fewer 1s as the aim gets closer to an axis.
ForceDirBoth: COP #AF with one byte operand (nonzero sets, zero clears). TSB or TRB bits $6000 on actor flags $12: negates both the X and Y deltas (reverses the staged movement).
ForceDirNE: COP #AE with one byte operand (nonzero sets, zero clears). TSB or TRB bit $2000 on actor flags $12: while set, the Y delta is negated (the copdef name says NE; the effect is a Y flip).
ForceDirSW: COP #AD with one byte operand (nonzero sets, zero clears). TSB or TRB bit $4000 on actor flags $12: while set, ApplyMovement and the collision-checked move negate the actor's X delta (the copdef name says SW; the effect is an X flip).
ForcedWalkEast: Same sequence as ForcedWalkSouth with ReadDirSprite_XVelocity and CameraPanRight.
ForcedWalkNorth: Same sequence as ForcedWalkSouth with ReadDirSprite_YVelocity and CameraPanUp.
ForcedWalkSouth:
Cutscene auto-walk actor spawned on the player by StartForcedWalk during extended warp transitions (default direction when no west/east/north bit is set).

Masks all joypad input, reads the first stream direction byte with ReadDirSprite_YVelocity, stages the player sprite, loads the walk sequence pointer from forced_walk_sequence_table into scrollStepTableBase, pans the camera down (CameraPanDown), applies the stream's position offset, reads the next direction byte, re-stages the sprite, syncs the player and dies. The North/West/East labels below follow the same sequence.
ForcedWalkWest: Same sequence as ForcedWalkSouth with ReadDirSprite_XVelocity and CameraPanLeft.
GenHdmaSine: COP #00 sine-wave HDMA table generator with no operands (2 sites: sine_hdma_ending_wave and the unused gen_hdma_sine_oneshot). First calls BuildSineLookupTable, which refills the two 256-word tables sineTableA ($7E8900) and sineTableB ($7E8B00, a copy directly after A) from the actor amplitude $7F0008, but only when displayModeFlags bit 6 or animScratch2 bit 0 requests it. Then it writes a 7-byte indirect HDMA table at $7E8800: [$FF, pointer, $E0, pointer+$FE, $00], i.e. 127 repeat-mode scanlines followed by 96 (223 in total), each scanline taking one word from a window of the sine data. spritesetPtr is a phase counter incremented on every call; the window starts at sineTableA + (counter AND $01FE), so the wave slides by one word every second call. It is not a double buffer. A following COP QueueHdma ($7E8800 with B-bus #0F or #10, i.e. BG2HOFS/BG2VOFS) binds the table to a channel.
GetPlayerFacing: COP #48 with no operands. Saves the script return address and calls GetPlayerFacingDirection; the facing value (0–3) is returned in accumulator A on RTI.
GiveItem: COP #D4 with one byte (item ID) and one &Code (overflow handler). Calls GiveItemToPlayer; on success (carry clear) skips the overflow branch, on failure (carry set, inventory full) jumps to the &Code overflow target. Side effects of GiveItemToPlayer: the item ID is stored at $0DB8 for the dialogue text, and Y returns a dialogue string pointer that this handler ignores (scripts show their own dialogue).
HaltIfMaxFrames: COP #69 with one word operand (frame threshold). Compares it with the global timeline counter $00E4 (mnemonic actorLimitThreshold; the ending-credits actors keep it running, e.g. code_09E919 in sF7_credits increments it each tick, and it is $FFFF while stopped). While the counter is NOT above the threshold (counter ≤ threshold, unsigned) the handler rewinds the actor's entry pointer ($00) to this COP, discards the COP frame and yields with RTL, so the COP runs again next tick. Once the counter is above the threshold the script continues via RTI. Used as a timeline wait in the ending credits.
HalveMovementDistance:
Iterative distance halver called by StageMove when the pixel distance high byte is non-zero.

Halves both moveXAlt and moveYAlt via LSR, then increments a halving-pass counter in chatPtr. StageMove calls this in a loop until the distance fits in a single byte, enabling the hardware divider to compute per-frame velocity accurately.
IncanRuinsTransformPaletteFinal: Final phase: kill sibling thinkers, fill CGRAM with transformed palette, loop #36
IncanRuinsTransformPaletteWarmup: Warmup phase: alternate between palette #34 and #33 until flag $FF clears
InitFollowAndChase:
Entry for helpers that start with no facing.

Same copy of loopCounter and chatPtr from the spawner as CopySiblingFollowState, then sets animScratch2 = $FFFF (facing not set) so the first ResolveFollowDirection snaps straight to the desired frame, and runs into FollowChaseMainLoop. The block also contains the two up-right handlers (the FollowChaseDiagQuadrantSW/NW and FollowChaseHeadNNE/ENE sub-labels): target up-right and Y dominant heads mostly north (facing base 0, X += minor, Y −= major), target up-right and X dominant heads mostly east (base 2, X += major, Y −= minor).
InitGravity: COP #63 with one signed byte (initial upward speed v0, sign-extended), one byte (shift factor f) and one byte (target Y tile offset). Stores v0 in scratch1010+2, f in scratch1010 and zeroes the tick counter scratch1010+4. The target Y is moveYAlt = $16 + offset × 16 (here moveYAlt holds a pixel Y, not a movement index, so a later StageMoveY on the same actor overwrites it). A negative offset byte ($80–$FF) is not sign-extended: the result is $16 − byte × 16. Every observed call uses offset #00.
InitSineHdma:
COP #5F with one word (WRAM table base) and one byte (wave period n, scanlines per HDMA entry). Builds the four indirect-HDMA tables described in the block note: 256/n entries each, line count n | $80 (repeat mode), every entry pointing at the same n data words at table + $0100. Scales the entry count with UnsignedDivide, caches the base in spritesetPtr and resets the delay counter (animScratch+2) and phase (retPtr1) to 0.

In this build the handler also stores the post-operand script pointer in the actor's $00/$02 entry fields before RTI (the two untagged LDA $0C / STA $02 / LDA $0A / STA $00 lines come from a transforms.json patch).
InitSmoothMovement:
Computes the interpolation setup for MoveToward on first entry.

Converts moveXAlt/moveYAlt from absolute target coordinates to distances from the current position ($14/$16), takes their absolute values, caps each at $00FE when the high byte is non-zero, and records the sign of each axis by ROR into $0004 (stored in animScratch2's high byte: bit 14 = X negative, bit 15 = Y negative). Selects the larger axis, divides it by the speed operand via UnsignedDivide to get the frame count, stores frames + 1 as the tick limit, zeroes the accumulators, tick counter and the override-chain pointers ($2C/$2E), and sets extendedFlags bit 1.
InitSpiral: COP #6C spiral-orbit initializer taking two byte operands: starting orbitDiameter and orbitAngle (256 units = one full turn). Stores them in the actor fields $7F0012/$7F0010 for the paired SpiralStep. Does not move the actor. mu67_vampires seeds quarter-turn angles #00/#40/#80/#C0 with diameter 0, then SpiralStep (#03, #02) grows the spiral until orbitDiameter ≥ $80.
IrqHandler: IRQ handler stub. Returns immediately via RTI since no hardware IRQ sources are enabled.
IrqVector: Hardware IRQ vector. Jumps to IrqHandler (currently a stub — hardware IRQs are unused).
JumpAfterDelay: COP #C3 with one Address (target) plus one word (frame delay). Sets actor $00/$02 to the target script pointer, stores the delay word in $08, and yields via RTL.
JumpFar: COP #C7 with one Address operand (word+bank). Cross-bank jump: writes the far entry to $00/$02 and updates the bank byte on the stack; RTI-resumes immediately at the target.
JumpNextFrame: COP #C4 with one Address operand. Sets $00/$02 to the target entry, zeroes the frame timer ($08), and yields via RTL for a one-frame deferred jump.
KillNext: COP #A9 with no operands. Switches context to the next linked actor ($06) and unlinks it via UnlinkActor. There is no null check, so the actor must have a next link.
KillPrev: COP #A8 with no operands. Switches context to the previous linked actor ($04) and unlinks it via UnlinkActor. There is no null check, so the actor must have a prev link.
KillThinker: COP #3D with no operands. Unlinks the calling thinker from the doubly-linked thinker list ($005A head / $005C tail), then returns its slot to the thinker free list (long pointer $52/$54): the pointer is backed up one word and the slot address stored there, the reverse of ThinkerPoolAlloc. When the removed thinker was the only one, $5C is not reset (it still names the freed slot).
loc_00EB85: Compute scroll deltas for the visual effect pipeline
LockPlayerForClimb:
Shared helper that freezes the player for a stair-climb animation sequence.

Takes the climb frame count from actor parameter $0E (shifted left twice into statsPtr at $7F0020), zeros player velocity words at $002C/$002E/$0008, masks directional joypad input ($0F00 in joypadMaskStd), and sets playerFlags bit $0800. Called by all four StairTrigger handlers immediately before the player script switches to a Climb* routine.
LoopEnd: COP #CB with no operands. Decrements the loop counter (pooled-actor or thinker variant). At zero it continues past the loop with RTI; otherwise it stores the count, sets $00 to the saved loop head and yields via RTL, so each iteration ends with a yield.
LoopStart:
COP #CA with one byte operand (iteration count). Stores the count and the loop-head PC (the address after the operand) and sets $00 to the loop head.

Pooled actors (X ≥ $1000) use loopCounter ($7F0014) and retPtr2 ($7F001E); thinkers (X < $1000) use loopCounterActor ($7F2102) and loopStartPcActor ($7F2100).
MainLoop:
The main game loop: one pass per frame, entered after SystemInit and never left (the last instruction is BRL MainLoop).

Order of one pass: VBlankWaitAndJoypad (frame sync and joypad read), EnableNmiOnly, RunThinkers_TypeA, CheckSceneTransition, CheckWarpAndChest, GlobalInputHandler, UpdateFrameCounters, RunActors_Normal, the $FF terminator for the OAM compose buffer, SortActorsByDepth, the four collision passes (RunCombatCollision, RunInteractionCollision, CheckPlayerDeath, ProcessDodgeCallbacks), CameraSmoothScroll for layer 0 and layer 1, ResetHdmaState, RunThinkers_TypeB, ComposeAllSprites, UpdateHUD, LoadMusicFromTransitionState, EnableNmiAndJoypad.
MarkChildActor:
Set the new actor's (Y) parentId: the spawner's (X) parentId if non-zero, otherwise the spawner's own slot (TDC).

Returns with X = D = the spawner again.
MarkCollisionRect: Internal JSR helper that marks a solid rectangle on the collision map. The actor's metasprite hitbox header (4 bytes at metaspritePtr, read in the sprite-data bank: X offset, Y offset, width in tiles, height in tiles) is combined with the pixel position in $0018/$001C (X/Y offsets are forced negative with ORA #$FF00), converted to a starting tile, and $F0 is ORed onto every collisionLayer byte of the rectangle. Columns step +1, crossing to the next 16-tile page with +$F0; rows step with AdvanceMapY. The whole rectangle is skipped if the starting index is ≥ $4000. Called only by MarkSolidHere (the other mark ops write a single tile).
MarkDeath: COP #A7 with no operands. Unlinks the actor via UnlinkActor; if actor flag bit $0040 on $12 is set, first cascade-unlinks child actors sharing the same parentId, then resumes the calling script via MarkDeathResumeHandler.
MarkDeathResumeHandler:
PEA/RTS return target reached from MarkDeath when the dying actor has child flag $0040 set.

Restores the actor's direct page (TCD) and index register (TAX) from the stack after the child-unlinking code in UnlinkChildrenCascade completes, then RTIs to resume the calling script. Separated from MarkDeath because the child-unlinking path is shared with Die via BRA UnlinkChildrenCascade.
MarkSolidAbs: COP #0F with two byte operands (absolute tile X and Y). Converts coordinates through TileCoordsToMapIndex and ORs #$F0 onto the collision byte at that index.
MarkSolidHere: COP #0B (legacy name SolidHighHere) collision marker with no operands. Copies the actor pixel position from $14/$16 into the probe scratch $18/$1C and calls MarkCollisionRect to OR $F0 onto every collision-layer tile covered by the actor's metasprite hitbox (the terrain nibble is preserved). The STZ $0000 beforehand is only meaningful to the Clear variants; MarkCollisionRect ignores it. Used by nearly every solid NPC, enemy and prop (462 call sites).
MarkSolidOffset: COP #0D with two signed byte operands (tile X/Y offsets). ParseSignedTileOffset sign-extends each offset, scales by 16 pixels, converts to tile coordinates (Y adjusted −16), then ORs #$F0 onto the single collisionLayer byte at that map index.
MovementVelocityCompute:
Per-axis velocity calculator for TickMove.

Writes the axis distance byte to WRMPYB, reads the multiply product from RDMPYL into WRDIVL, divides by animScratch2−1 (frame count) via WRDIVB, waits 5 NOPs for divider latency, then returns the per-frame pixel step in A ($0000). Called twice per TickMove tick: once for Y axis, once for X axis.
MoveToward:
COP #22 with two byte operands (animation index, speed in px/frame). The target is in moveXAlt/moveYAlt, set by the script beforehand.

On first entry InitSmoothMovement computes the distances and the frame count and sets extendedFlags bit 1; each later call moves the actor by the next per-axis delta and yields RTL until the tick counter ($24) reaches the limit (frames + 1). Usage in extracted/: speeds 1, 2, 3, 4 and 8.
MoveTowardFinish:
Cleanup exit for MoveToward when the frame counter matches the target tick count.

Clears extendedFlags bit 1 (smooth move active) via AND #$FFFD, skips the two-byte operand by advancing $0A, and yields RTL to resume the calling script. Called via JMP from MoveToward when animScratch2 low byte equals $24.
MultiplyThenDivide:
Chained hardware multiply→divide giving the offset travelled by this tick.

WRMPYA holds the tick counter ($24, set by the caller). Writes the axis distance byte to WRMPYB (starting the multiply), copies the product from RDMPYL into WRDIVL as the dividend, divides by animScratch2−1 (the frame count) via WRDIVB and returns the quotient in A and $0000: the cumulative pixels moved by this tick. The caller subtracts the previous accumulator to get this frame's delta. When the divisor is zero (distance < speed) the divide is skipped and 0 is returned. Called twice per MoveToward tick (X and Y).
MusicAndText: COP #19 with one byte (track ID), one word (text pointer), and one byte (data bank). On pool success, allocates via ActorPoolAllocator, copies actor state, sets MusicJingleActor, and stores operands in $0026/$0020/$0022. On pool exhaustion, falls back to inline DialogStringRenderer with temporary data bank, joypad input suppressed, and displayModeFlags bit $80 cleared.
NmiHandler:
V-Blank interrupt handler — the per-frame DMA orchestration routine.

Execution order:
1. Save registers, data bank = $81
2. Disable HDMA (HDMAEN = 0) to avoid bus conflicts
3. UploadScrollRegisters
4. FlushDirtyTilemapStrips (dirty column/row data)
5. UploadCgramPalette (512 bytes from $7F0A00)
6. UploadOamTable (544 bytes from $0422)
7. Bg3TilemapVramDma: partial BG3 upload when displayModeFlags bit 4/5 is set
8. VMAIN = $80, BBAD0 = $18, DMAP0 = $01 (word writes to VRAM)
9. If displayModeFlags bit 3 is set: DmaPlayerTilesToVram only. Otherwise DmaAdhocVramBlock, FlushVramWriteQueue and ExecuteVramDma; with dmaSkipFlag set, only FlushVramWriteQueue
10. Re-enable the HDMA channels from the mask in $66
11. Spin until the joypad auto-read finishes, store JOY1L in joypadRaw
12. If musicTransitionState is positive (SPC music upload in progress in the main loop): run UpdateFrameFull
13. Otherwise write APUIO2: 0 on odd frames, the dequeued sfxQueueCh1 byte on even frames
14. Increment the frame parity counter ($36) and restore registers
NmiVector: NMI (V-Blank) interrupt vector. Jumps to the NMI handler for per-frame DMA transfers and display updates.
NudgePosition: COP #BC with two signed byte operands (delta X, delta Y). Sign-extends each byte and adds the offsets to the actor's pixel position at $14/$16.
OamFillConstant_unused: Single-byte constant ($E0) used as the fixed DMA source by OamFillE0_unused (which has no caller). $E0 = 224 puts a sprite just below the 224-line display.
OamFillE0_unused:
Fills the OAM staging buffer at WRAM $0422 with the byte $E0 via DMA.

Uses DMA fixed-source mode ($08) to repeat one byte across 512 bytes (128 OAM entries × 4 bytes) through the WRAM data port ($2180). $E0 puts every sprite Y at 224, below the visible area.

Unreferenced: no caller of OamFillE0_unused was found in extracted/.
OrExtraFlags: COP #5B with one word operand. ORs the value into the actor's extendedFlags word at $7F002A.
PaletteResetAndKillThinker:
Thinker script body (spawned with COP SpawnThinkerParam, about a dozen callers): COP PaletteRestart, PaletteStep, then KillThinker.

Resets the palette fade machinery for one frame and removes the thinker.
PaletteRestart: COP #36 with no operands. Restarts the bundle whose ID is already in animScratch+2: branches into the shared tail of PaletteStart (loc_009370), which zeroes the sub-entry index, loads and applies sub-entry 0, saves the resume address and yields. It does not set the bundle ID itself (not "bundle 0"): ambient thinkers get it from their spawn parameter, and the 2 sites are ambient_palette_cycler and PaletteResetAndKillThinker (actor_pool).
PaletteStart: COP #37 with one byte operand (palette bundle ID, 84 sites). Stores the ID in animScratch+2, zeroes the sub-entry index ($0E), loads sub-entry 0 with LoadPaletteBundle and applies it with DecompressGfxToVram. Then stores the address after the operand in $00 (the actor entry point) and yields with PLA, PLA, RTL, so the next frame resumes at the following op (normally PaletteStep).
PaletteStartLoop: COP #38 with two byte operands (bundle ID, pass count). Stores the ID in animScratch+2 and the pass count in retPtr1, zeroes the sub-entry index, applies sub-entry 0 and yields exactly like PaletteStart. The count is the TOTAL number of passes PaletteStepLoop makes through the bundle (a count of 0 would give 65,536 passes, by the DEC in StepLoop). Only 3 sites use it: two attack_ability_system effects (#2A/#4B with 2 passes) and one unused script.
PaletteStep: COP #39 with no operands (85 sites). Decrements the hold counter in spritesetPtr once per call. While it is still nonzero the counter is stored back, the current data pointer (animScratch) is copied to $08 and DecompressGfxToVram runs again, then the actor yields (the entry point saved by PaletteStart makes the same Step op run next frame). When the counter reaches zero LoadPaletteBundle loads the next sub-entry: carry clear = another frame, which is applied and the actor yields; carry set = end of bundle, so the script continues past this op with RTI and the sub-entry index has been reset to 0.
PaletteStepLoop: COP #3A with no operands. Same hold/frame logic as PaletteStep, but when LoadPaletteBundle reports the end of the bundle it decrements the pass counter in retPtr1: if nonzero it is stored and the bundle restarts at once (LoadPaletteBundle already reset the sub-entry index), and only when the counter reaches zero does the script continue with RTI. Pairs with PaletteStartLoop, which sets retPtr1.
ParseMapEntry:
Decodes a 3-byte stream record at address X into tile coordinates and metatile ID.

Zeroes direct page, reads 3 bytes from the stream: byte 0 = tile X, byte 1 = tile Y, byte 2 = metatile ID. If byte 0 has bit 7 set, returns carry set (end-of-stream sentinel). Otherwise sign-extends tile coords, computes pixel positions (×16) in DP $1A/$1E, stores tile coords in DP $18/$1C and metatile ID in DP $00, and returns carry clear. Called by WorldMapStream3/4 for sequential tile painting.
ParseSignedTileOffset: Internal JSR helper that reads two signed byte operands from the script pointer at $0A (D = actor slot). Sign-extends each offset, scales by 16 pixels, adds them to the actor position ($14/$16, with Y reduced by $10, one tile row), and converts the result to tile coordinates in $0018/$001C. Returns via RTS with $0A advanced past both operands. Called only by MarkSolidOffset and ClearSolidOffset; BranchIfSolidOffset repeats the arithmetic inline in pixel units.
PlaySoundBoth: COP #08 with one word operand (two SFX bytes packed). Stores the entire 16-bit value to sfxQueueCh1 as a word, filling both $06F8 and $06F9 in one write.
PlaySoundCh1: COP #07 with one byte operand (SFX ID). Writes the byte directly to sfxQueueCh1 ($06F8) for channel-1 sound effect playback.
PlaySoundCh2: COP #06 with one byte operand (SFX ID). Writes the byte directly to sfxQueueCh2 ($06F9) for channel-2 sound effect playback.
PrintDialogString:
COP #BF with one word operand (text pointer).

Sets displayModeFlags bit 13 ($2000; no reader found), calls UpdateFrameRender to sync the display, clears actor $10 bit 11 and joypadMaskStd, renders the text via DialogStringRenderer, then restores the mask, re-applies it to joypadCurrent (TRB) and clears the D-pad bits ($0F00) in joypadHeld.
PrintDialogStringAlt:
COP #6B with one word operand (text pointer).

Like PrintDialogString but without the bit 13 set/clear and the UpdateFrameRender sync, and it does not re-apply the mask to joypadCurrent; it still clears actor $10 bit 11 and joypadMaskStd while rendering and clears the D-pad bits in joypadHeld afterwards.
ProcessAnimFlag: Internal JSR helper shared by all StageSpriteFrame variants. Clears frame counter $2A, then interprets the animation index byte: $FF leaves $28 unchanged (no-op), bit $80 set masks to the low 7 bits and conditionally sets horizontal flip ($4000 on $0E) based on actor flag $0002, and all other values store directly to $28 while clearing the flip bit. Returns via RTS.
QueueDma: COP #02 (28 sites). Same operands as QueueHdma (3-byte table address, B-bus register byte; used for window position registers #26, mode 7 matrix registers #1B–#1E, scroll registers and others). It calls SetupHdmaChannel_Direct, which writes DMAP WITHOUT the $40 flag and still sets the channel's bit in the HDMA enable mask, so this is a DIRECT-table HDMA channel (each table entry holds the register data inline), not a general linear DMA transfer. The name QueueDma is misleading; QueueHdma is the indirect variant.
QueueHdma: COP #01 (18 sites). Operands: a 3-byte table address (word + bank, e.g. $7E8800 or @label) and a byte naming the PPU B-bus register ($21xx, e.g. #0F = BG2HOFS). The handler reads them as two words: Y = address, A = bank (low byte) | register (high byte). SetupHdmaChannel_Indirect then picks the DMAP transfer mode from hdma_channel_config[register], ORs $40 (indirect addressing), uses the bank for both the table and the indirect data, and binds the NEXT free channel (allocated from channel 1 upward via $68/$6A; reset by ResetHdmaState). The channel is armed through the HDMA enable mask ($66).
QueueHdmaChannel: COP #03 (2 sites, both in scene_lifecycle: channels 6 and 7 for the BG1/BG2 horizontal scroll window). Operands: a byte channel number (0–7), a 3-byte table address, and a byte B-bus register. Unlike #01/#02 it programs the named channel directly: register block offset = channel × 16 ($4300 + offset), channel bit ORed into the HDMA enable mask $66, DMAP = hdma_channel_config[register] | $40 (indirect), DASB = A1B = bank, BBAD = register, A1T = table address. The handler PHYs the slot and PLXes it back at the end instead of using TYX, and uses WRAM $0000/$0002 as scratch.
QueueMapChange:
COP #26 with one byte (scene ID), two words (spawn X, Y), one byte (flags) and one word (scroll parameters). Writes sceneNext ($0642), warpDestX/Y ($064C/$064E), warpFacing ($0650, the flags byte) and warpScrollParams ($0652).

If flags bit 7 is set it is cleared in warpFacing and the address of this operand block (PC − 8) and its bank are stored in sceneSaveData and reviveWarpPtr. The operand block has the layout of a warp record (entry+4 in the warp table), and game_over_sequence reloads from these pointers, so bit 7 marks the scene change as the new revive/save point; nothing resumes at that address as script code.
ReadDirSprite_XVelocity: Same as ReadDirSprite_YVelocity, but the velocity-curve pointer goes to $2C (X axis) instead of $2E.
ReadDirSprite_YVelocity:
Read the next walk-step stream byte and set up the sprite and the Y velocity curve for it.

Y = stream pointer (warpFacing, $0650), incremented by one. The byte indexes direction_velocity_table (word entries): the whole word goes to $0000 (low byte = animation index used by StagePlayerSprFromDP); its high byte indexes movement_delta_table, and that pointer (head of a delta-node velocity list) is stored in $2E. ReadDirSprite_XVelocity is identical but stores it in $2C.
ReadDivideResult: Hardware divide latency wrapper. Five NOPs provide the 16-cycle wait required after writing WRDIVB before the SNES hardware divider result is valid, then reads RDDIVL into A. Called by MultiplyThenDivide.
ReadMultiplyResult: Hardware multiply latency wrapper. One NOP provides the 8-cycle wait required after writing WRMPYB before the SNES hardware multiplier result is valid, then reads RDMPYL into Y. Called by MultiplyThenDivide.
ReloadMoveDurations: COP #B1 with no operands. Re-runs AnimFrameLookup for the current moveXAlt and moveYAlt and stores the chain pointers in $2C and $2E again, rewinding both chains to their first node.
RemoveItem: COP #D5 with one byte operand (item ID). Calls RemoveItemFromInventory (zeroes the matching slot and, as a side effect, resets the equipped state: inventoryEquippedType = 0, inventoryEquippedIndex = $FFFF) and continues.
ResetSpriteState: COP #55 (script name ResetSpriteInit) sprite/animation reset taking one byte and one word operand. Stores the animation index in $28, clears the frame counter $2A, and sets the spriteset/script bank pointer $24. Does not advance animation itself — it reinitializes state before StageSpriteFrame/AnimOnce sequences.
ResetVector: CPU reset entry point. Disables interrupts, clears carry, switches from 65816 emulation mode to native mode via XCE, then jumps long to SystemInit.
ResolveActorIndex: Internal JSR helper that converts an 8-bit actor list index in A to a WRAM actor pointer in Y. Computes Y = index × $30 + $1000 using Multiply8x8Unsigned, matching the fixed $30-byte actor structure layout. Called by BranchIfActorNear and BranchIfActorAt before distance or coordinate comparisons.
ResolveFollowDirection:
Picks the desired facing frame and turns toward it. Desired = ($0000 base + offset) & 15, where the offset comes from the slope row in orbitAngle: row ≥ $0D → 0, $05-$0C → 1, < 5 → 2; ResolveFollowDirectionAlt (next block) swaps offsets 0 and 2.

The shared tail (sub-labels in the Alt block) then compares it with animScratch2 (the current facing, 16 frames clockwise from north): $FFFF (unset) or within one frame snaps to the desired frame and sets $0000 = $FFFF (aligned); otherwise the facing moves one frame the short way round (a half-turn counts as counter-clockwise). Unless chatPtr bit 15 is set, the spawner's animation becomes chatPtr + facing ($28, frame counter $2A = 0) and UpdateActorAnimation is run for it. Finally it jumps through FollowDirectionTable to the FollowDirHandler for the new facing, with carry = chatPtr bit 15.
ResolveFollowDirectionAlt: Alt entry of ResolveFollowDirection with offsets 0 and 2 swapped (row ≥ $0D → 2, < 5 → 0). The normal entry is used by the handlers whose base frame is an axis frame (N, E, S, W: axis-aligned row = base), the Alt entry by those whose base is a diagonal frame (NE, SE, SW, NW: axis-aligned row = base + 2). The labels ResolveFollowDirMoveXOnly/Diagonal/MoveYOnly describe the normal entry only.
ResolveTileData:
Converts parsed tile coordinates to a map-layer index and writes metatile and collision data.

Calls TileCoordsToMapIndex (DP $18/$1C → linear index in X), reads the collision byte from animScratch[index], writes the metatile ID to mapLayerTilemap[index] and collision byte to collisionLayer[index]. Then checks if the tile is on-screen by comparing pixel X against BG1 scroll and pixel Y against BG2 scroll. When visible, expands the metatile into four 16×16 VRAM tile words from metatileMapLayer, stages them in the tile-update queue ($0904–$090C), and computes the VRAM address pair via PixelToVramAddress. Called by DrawMetatileAbs/Here and WorldMapStream3/4.
RestorePlayerControl:
Restores normal player locomotion after a climb or ramp animation finishes.

Resets the player actor entry pointer to PlayerIdleEntry, clears velocity scratch at $002C/$002E/$0008, adjusts status word $0010 (clears $0200, sets $0008), unmasks joypad ($0F00), and clears playerFlags $0800. Called from UnlockPlayerAfterClimb and from ramp exit handlers in ramps.asm.
RestoreSavedPtr: COP #C5 with no operands. If retPtr1 ($7F0004) is non-zero, restores it as the script PC and clears retPtr1; otherwise yields via RTL.
ResumeAfterSnap: COP #4A with no operands. Restores the saved script PC and bank from snapResumePtr ($7F1018) and $7F101A after grid snapping completes, then clears both save slots.
ReturnActorSlot:
Push actor slot X back on the free list and decrement the counters (JSR; D must equal X).

Zeroes D so the free-list pointer ($4E) can be used as [$4E], backs the pointer up by 2 with an 8-bit DEC (no borrow; safe because the whole list sits inside page $0E), decrements activeActorCount, stores X into the freed entry and finally sets D = X again, undoing its own TCD #0.
ReturnWithSignal: COP #E1 with no operands. Restores the deferred call PC from retPtr1 (clearing it); if set, RTI-resumes with A=$FFFF as a non-zero signal to the caller, otherwise yields via RTL.
RngByte:
COP #23 with no operands. Steps a 16-byte additive generator over $0410–$041F and returns the new $0410 byte in A.

For X = 15..1: byte[$040F+X] += byte[$0410+X] + carry (one carry chain, so $041E += $041F first and $0410 += $0411 last). Then a ripple counter at $041F is incremented, carrying toward lower addresses. rngState ($040F) is the index base; $040F itself is never touched.
RngMod:
COP #24 with one byte operand (modulus). Reduces the current RngByte output ($0410) by repeated subtraction and stores the remainder in rngModuloResult ($0420). Does not advance the generator.

A modulus of 0 would loop forever (the subtraction never goes negative); extracted/ uses $50 and $60.
RunBg3Script:
COP #BD BG3 console-script runner taking one Address operand: a far pointer to a BG3 tilemap command stream.

Switches the data bank, calls ConsoleStringRenderer with the direct page zeroed, then sets displayModeFlags bit 0 (full BG3 staging-buffer upload request). Used by the diary menu, title screen and boot-logo actors, and by UpdateHUD for the HUD counters.
RunPlayerAnim: COP #93 with no operands. Calls UpdateActorAnimation once per script tick; clears $2C/$2E when the animation finishes (carry set). Yields via RTL while the animation is still running.
ScrollCameraAccumulate:
Accumulative camera scroll actor-def used in Pyramid interior scenes.

Zeroes the accumulators at DP $24 (X) and $26 (Y), packs the position via TileAlignPosition, then each frame calls ComputeScrollDeltas and adds the accumulators to cameraDeltaX and cameraDeltaY. Other actors can write $24/$26 to add drift on top of the standard tracking.
ScrollCameraInit:
Camera initialization scroll actor (spawn #DF, #DF; Mt. Kress scenes).

Sets bit 12 ($1000) in the actor status word, subtracts 8 px (X) and 16 px (Y) from the position parameters and packs both with TileAlignCoord into the multiplier/divisor words $14/$16.

Runs COP LoopStart with count 3 around ComputeScrollDeltas; all three passes use the same inputs, so they give the same result. After the loop, copies cameraDeltaY to effectScrollV ($0690).

Then sets the re-entry point (COP SetEntryHere), computes the deltas again each frame, ORs bit 15 into cameraDeltaX and stores it in forcedScrollOverride ($06C8), and zeroes cameraDeltaX. Outside visual_effect_pipeline no reader of $06C8 was found in extracted/ (OQ-57).
ScrollCameraTrack:
Simple continuous camera tracking actor.

Sets bit 12 of the status word, packs the spawn position via TileAlignPosition, then re-runs ComputeScrollDeltas every frame (after COP SetEntryHere) with the current camera targets.

The default camera actor: about 100 scene spawns use it (87 of them with #11, #11).
ScrollCameraVertical:
Vertical-only camera tracking actor-def referenced from scene_actors in Edward's Castle, Itory, Incan Ruins and Dao.

Sets bit 12, packs the position via TileAlignPosition, then every frame computes only the Y delta through MulDivide when $16 is nonzero. cameraDeltaX is left unchanged and the X parameter ($14) is ignored. Three of its spawns use #21, #00, whose Y parameter is 0, so they compute nothing (OQ-57).
SelectFallbackDirection: Entered while the facing is still turning ($0000 not yet $FFFF). A = heading 1-8 stored in $0000 by the FollowDirHandler; (A − 1) & 7 indexes follow_fallback_table, whose entries are the apply halves of the eight octant handlers (headings N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW), so the actor keeps moving along its current facing with the slope row the handler set.
SetActorBody:
Apply the current characterForm's body_table entry to actor X (JSR helper).

Index = form × 6 (each body_table entry is 6 bytes). Writes the spriteset pointer ($7F0006) and bank ($7F0008), then clears playerFlags bit $8000, the sprite-override flag (set by SetPlayerSpriteDirect, see GetPlayerFacingDirection).
SetCollideCallback: COP #5A with one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in onCollideCallback ($7F1008) for collision-event dispatch.
SetCollisionAbs: COP #42 (legacy name SetSolidAbs) absolute collision writer taking three byte operands: tile X, tile Y, and a full collision-layer byte value. Converts the tile coordinates through TileCoordsToMapIndex and stores the byte directly into collisionLayer, replacing both nibbles (solid and type) in one write. Used once in the game. The handler has no TYX: it pushes Y (the slot) at entry and recovers it with PLX at the end, after X has been used for the map index.
SetCustomCallback: COP #5E with one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in the custom-callback word ($7F1016, written as scratch1010+6) of the actor's slot. combat_collision runs it as the interaction handler for push hits; some actors reuse the word for other data.
SetDeathCallback: COP #57 with an @Code far-pointer operand (word + bank byte, 3 bytes). Stores the word in onDeathCallback ($7F1004) and the bank in the following word ($7F1006), both indexed by actor slot, for the death script hook.
SetDodgeCallback: COP #59 with one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in onDodgeCallback ($7F1002) for dodge-event dispatch.
SetDungeonKillFlag: COP #D8 with no script operands. Reads the actor's enemyNum ($7F:0022,X — the dungeon enemy number used for kill tracking) as a flag index and, when its low byte is non-zero, calls SetWramFlag to set that bit in the wramFlags bitfield ($0A80), recording the kill (cleared only as described in flag_helpers, OQ-67). Index 0 is ignored.
SetEntryFar: COP #E2 with one Address operand (word + bank). Writes the far entry pointer to $00/$02 and zeroes $08, then RTI-continues in the current stream without yielding. Unlike JumpFar it does not jump: the new entry only takes effect the next time the actor resumes.
SetEntryHere: COP #C1 with no operands. Saves the current script bank ($0C→$02) and PC ($0A→$00) as the actor entry/resume pointer without yielding.
SetEntryHereAndYield: COP #C2 with no operands. Same entry-pointer save as SetEntryHere, then pops the return address and yields via RTL so execution resumes next frame.
SetEventFlag: Core JSR routine that sets one bit in the eventFlags ($0A00) bitfield. Decomposes the flag index into byte (÷8) and bit (AND $07) indices, ORs the bitmasks_bit_position entry into the eventFlags byte. Called by all SetFlag COP handlers and JSL offset wrappers.
SetEventFlag_0200: JSL helper that sets persistent event flag $0200 + A (bytes $0A40–$0A5F) via SetEventFlag. A is not masked, so callers must pass a 0–$FF index. Callers: warps_interaction (chest opened) and hidden_red_jewel.
SetFlag_0100: JSL helper that sets event/trigger flag $0100 + (A AND $FF), bytes $0A20–$0A3F (callers: StandardEnemyDefeatHandler, EnemyDefeatDispatch, wall walker, mystic ball).
SetFlag_0300: JSL helper that sets event flag $0300 + (A AND $FF); used to mark a scene's clear reward as claimed (reward_actors, boss_clear_reward_handler).
SetFlagByte: COP #CC with one byte operand (flag index). Calls SetEventFlag to OR the corresponding bit in the eventFlags ($0A00) bitfield.
SetFlagRaw: JSL helper that sets an event flag without adding a base offset. Masks to byte and calls SetEventFlag directly.
SetFlagWord: COP #CD with one word operand (flag index). Calls SetEventFlag with the 16-bit flag number.
SetHitCallback: COP #58 with one &Code operand. Stores the script pointer in onHitCallback ($7F1000) for hit-event dispatch.
SetHMirror: COP #BB with no operands. Sets horizontal mirror bit $4000 on OAM attribute word $0E via TSB.
SetInteractHandler: COP #C0 with one &Code operand. Stores it in the actor's chatPtr ($7F000A), the routine the interaction system runs when the player talks to or touches the actor. Used by NPCs, chests and inspectable objects (322 uses). The copdef name is SetInteractHandler; 'SetOnInteract' is only a stale name in the docs.
SetLinkedEntryPtr:
COP $6A (SetLinkedEntryPtr) with one &Code operand: point the next-linked actor ($06) at a new script.

Only the 16-bit word at the linked actor's $00/$01 is replaced (the 2-byte operand is a same-bank pointer; its bank byte $02 is left as it was), and its waitCounter ($08) and moveX/moveY ($2C/$2E) are zeroed so the new script starts on the linked actor's next tick with no pending wait or velocity.
